description: Exact natural-language provenance rules and production calibration cases. Every case is prompt-visible and a regression contract; known-wrong narratives mark adjacent factual and presentation failures.

rules.title: Read the complete retained lineage
rules.invariant: Use the complete frozen Trace component in chronological order; do not reduce provenance to the latest event or latest recorded reason.

rules.title: Explain the origin context
rules.invariant: When a selected Memory was derived from a larger Memory, state the selected content's meaningful role or placement within that source and preserve the specific nearby context needed to understand why the fragment existed.

rules.title: Name how the standalone Memory arose
rules.invariant: State the recorded operation and material method that produced the selected Memory, such as sentence chunking, without replacing it with a generic created label.

rules.title: Narrate disappearance and return
rules.invariant: Preserve every selected-Memory presence, content, or position transition needed to explain when it disappeared, returned, changed, or was finally removed.

rules.title: Keep sibling activity out
rules.invariant: A component event that changes only a parent, child, or sibling Memory is context, not a lifecycle transition of the selected Memory, and must not be narrated as though it happened to the selected Memory.

rules.title: Write prose, not an event log
rules.invariant: Synthesize one chronological natural-language paragraph; do not expose raw event labels, arrows, checkpoint identifiers, timestamps, transition counts, or a command inventory.

rules.title: Compress without truncating facts
rules.invariant: Use one or two complete sentences within the requested character, UTF-8 byte, or whitespace-delimited word limit. Merge repeated subjects and paired undo/redo clauses, but retain origin context, derivation mechanism, and final lifecycle state; never mechanically clip a generated sentence.

rules.title: Do not invent intent
rules.invariant: A directly supported textual role such as a hesitation may be described from wording and placement, but do not claim that the author intended a placeholder, judged content useless, or had another unrecorded motive.

rules.title: Keep unavailable provenance explicit
rules.invariant: Return no narrative when retained history is absent or hidden by a Grant; never fill either condition from current content or outside knowledge.

expected.provenance: “Um...” began as a hesitation between a minimal-change instruction and its “distribute, not divide” example. Sentence chunking made it a standalone Memory; undo removed it, redo restored it, and remove later deleted it.

known_wrong.provenance: CREATED via chunk → REMOVED via undo → RESTORED via redo → REMOVED via remove
known_wrong.reason: The event chain omits the parent instruction and example, and exposes internal labels instead of explaining the provenance.
The latest recorded reason neither explains the fragment's source context nor its later disappearance and return.

known_wrong.provenance: The author deliberately inserted a disposable placeholder, which was removed because it was useless.
known_wrong.reason: The Trace supports a hesitation's wording and placement but records neither placeholder intent nor a usefulness judgment.

known_wrong.provenance: After removal, the Memory was preserved by Atomize.
known_wrong.reason: The later Atomize events contain only the preceding and following sibling UIDs.

cases.description: A directly added Memory is removed and restored when that removal is undone.

expected.provenance: This Memory was added directly, later removed, and restored when that removal was undone.

known_wrong.reason: The endpoint alone hides both the removal and its undo.
